correctness.rationale: The published rank-four seed supplies the target disc. Adding any number of Jordan three-blocks and at most one Jordan two-block preserves partial-isometry status, adds exactly the required rank, and does not enlarge the numerical range after the center is restricted so that both centered Jordan discs lie inside the seed disc. The parity calculation gives the stated dimension formula, and zero padding handles larger dimensions. The published low-rank theorem gives impossibility through rank three.

evidence: Together these sources supply every substantive ingredient: seed, lower-rank impossibility, contained padding discs and direct-sum behavior.

originality.rationale: The rank-four seed and the sharp impossibility through rank three are published. Once the rank-four disc is known, the claimed all-higher-rank existence follows routinely from two classical facts: nilpotent Jordan shifts are partial isometries with centered disc numerical ranges, and numerical ranges of direct sums are convex hulls of the summand ranges. Copies of the rank-two and rank-one Jordan shifts can realize every extra rank while their discs sit strictly inside the published seed disc. Under the audit rule that direct corollaries assembled from prior results are covered even without identical wording, the higher-rank half does not clear originality.

final_claim: A finite-dimensional real partial isometry has a nondegenerate off-center circular numerical range at some rank exactly when the rank is at least four; the assigned block construction gives the stated sufficient ambient dimension for every such rank.
